beforeCommit.message:
feat(ui): add a cross-platform selectable dates rule to AdaptiveDatePicker

Closes #328.

The docs advertised a dateValidator parameter that never existed.
AdaptiveDatePickerState now exposes an observable selectableDates rule
that works on every platform, plus DateBounds, a SelectableDates for a
minimum and maximum day (inclusive, compared per UTC day), and an infix
`and` to combine rules.

- Material: the Material3 state is wrapped so it reports the caller's
  rule object; Material3 caches each day's enabled flag keyed on that
  object, so a rule changing its answers in place would never redraw
- iOS 16+ inline picker: backed by UICalendarView, whose selection
  delegate greys out days the rule rejects; bounds coming from a
  DateBounds map to the available date range, and the visible days are
  rebuilt after every change so it shows immediately rather than on the
  next scroll or tap
- iOS wheels picker and inline below iOS 16: backed by UIDatePicker,
  which only supports min/max, so DateBounds stop the wheels and any
  other rejected pick snaps to the nearest selectable day
- A selection the new rule rejects is moved to the nearest selectable
  day on every platform; the state is the source of truth and the
  native view follows it
- Saver re-attaches the rule and restores lists saved before it existed
- Year bounds use a dependency-free days-to-civil year calculation
- Tests: DateBoundsTest, DateBoundsSelectableDatesTest (commonTest) and
  AdaptiveDatePickerStateMaterialTest (desktopTest, incl. a Compose
  recomposition re-sync test)
- Docs rewritten with multiplatform examples; sample shows one picker
  with a range chip row and a weekdays-only toggle

beforeCommit.message:
feat(ui): add AdaptiveCompactDatePicker and AdaptiveDateRangePicker

Two more date pickers sharing the bounds and selectable-dates rule.

AdaptiveCompactDatePicker: a field showing the selected date that opens
the calendar on tap. Material platforms show an outlined button that
opens a DatePickerDialog editing a scratch state, so the shared state
only changes on confirm; iOS uses the native compact UIDatePicker, which
is measured again after each selection because its label resizes. It takes
the same AdaptiveDatePickerState as the inline picker.

AdaptiveDateRangePicker with AdaptiveDateRangePickerState: one common
state class wrapping Material3's DateRangePickerState on every platform.
Material platforms show the Material3 DateRangePicker. iOS 16+ shows a
native UICalendarView with multi-date selection driven by a pure
DateRangeSelection reducer (first tap sets the start, a tap on or after
it sets the end, a tap before it moves the start, any tap on a complete
range starts over); every day of the range is highlighted and rejected
days are greyed out. Below iOS 16 the Material3 picker is shown. The
Material picker scrolls its months and cannot take an unbounded height,
so inside a scrolling column it falls back to DateRangePickerFallbackHeight
instead of crashing.

- iOS: DatePickerManager gains presentations (inline, wheels, compact),
  an enabled flag and an intrinsic size; the UICalendarView setup is
  shared by a CalendarViewHost; the state-to-native sync composable is
  shared by the inline and compact pickers; native pickers are keyed on
  their state so taps never reach a stale instance
- StateBackedSelectableDates replaces the Material-only helper so the
  single and range states share it
- Tests: DateRangeSelectionTest (commonTest),
  AdaptiveDateRangePickerStateTest and
  AdaptiveCompactDatePickerMaterialTest (desktopTest, Compose UI)
- Docs: compact and range picker sections; sample rebuilt with compact,
  range and inline sections driven by one set of range and rule controls
